key_insight: PhySeqNet uses physics-informed synthetic training to detect dense fluorescent BARseq foci without manual annotations, improving sensitivity in challenging overlapping-signal tissue images.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical, modular detector that can be dropped into BARseq pipelines to increase transcript recovery while preserving downstream biological interpretation.
method: Train U-Net detectors on semi-synthetic images built from an instrument-matched optical model plus real experimental noise
Use annotation-free learning in place of unreliable manual ground truth from real tissue
Apply barcode-aware non-maxima suppression and integrate the model into pyBARseq
evidence_signal: On held-out simulations PhySeqNet performed strongly across wavelength bands, and on real tissue it achieved better reconstruction fidelity than BarDensr, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning baseline, with 51 median counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr.
watch_item: Because evaluation on real tissue relies on forward-model reconstruction rather than direct ground truth, performance may depend on how accurately the optical/noise simulation matches the imaging setup.
paper_title: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
